page: Microsoft Azure D96_v5 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the Dv5 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The configuration features 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall within the average range, multi-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% on stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is also strong, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 5005.56 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 325.48 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is particularly notable, with the Passmark CPU encryption test ranking in the top 10% tier, aided by hardware-accelerated instructions like AES and SHA-NI.

The qualitative cost profile of the D96_v5 reflects its high resource density, offering a substantial pool of compute and memory resources on a single virtual machine. However, the complete absence of local storage means users must rely entirely on external network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy operations. The instance provides a balanced resource-to-compute ratio, making it a stable platform for workloads that scale horizontally across many threads rather than those requiring extreme single-core clock speeds or local NVMe performance.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark strengths, the D96_v5 is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale language model inference. It is also applicable for general-purpose enterprise applications, containerized microservices, and memory-conscious batch processing tasks that do not require local disk storage.
